abstentions.reason: Generic risk-factor boilerplate: a hypothetical that the company may be party to litigation in the normal course of business, with no stated driver state, change, guidance or action, so the gate drops it.

Generic risk boilerplate: an undifferentiated statement that unknown or currently immaterial risks could adversely affect the business, naming no driver state, change, surprise, guidance or action, so the gate drops it.

Generic risk-factor boilerplate: a hypothetical crash that 'could expose us to significant liability' names no current, source-flagged specific threat and states no driver state, change, guidance or action, so the gate drops it.
Generic forward-looking risk-factor boilerplate listing a possible effect of aircraft accidents; it states no driver state, change, surprise, guidance or action, so the gate drops it.
Generic filing boilerplate stating that no material changes occurred to the Form 10-K risk factors; it reports no driver state, change, surprise, guidance or action, so the du_worthy gate drops it.

The passage states only a change in how hedge settlement gains and losses on Monroe inventory are presented inside non-GAAP adjusted results; a measurement-definition and presentation change belongs to measurement, never a driver name, and no driver's state, change, guidance, surprise or business action is reported, so no lawful fact can be named.
Generic forward-looking-statements safe-harbor boilerplate: it names no driver and states no state, change, surprise, guidance or action, so the gate drops it.

Generic forward-looking risk boilerplate listing fuel price changes, fuel price volatility, and fuel availability as factors that could affect results; it states no driver state, change, surprise, guidance, or action, so the gate drops it.

The sentence only defines the company's use of the term 'constant currency' as a non-GAAP presentation convention; it reports no driver state, change, surprise, guidance or action, so the du_worthy gate drops it as methodology boilerplate.
Generic safe-harbor / forward-looking-statements legal boilerplate: it states no driver state, change, surprise, guidance, or action, so the gate yields no record.
Generic risk-factor boilerplate: it says litigation may adversely affect the business without stating any specific current litigation, its stage, size, or any change in state, so the gate drops it.

Segment-reporting presentation note: it states only where Chuy's sales and profits are classified for reporting, giving no driver state, change, surprise, guidance or action, so the gate yields no DriverUpdate.
Generic forward-looking risk-factor boilerplate listing litigation and unfavorable publicity as things that could hurt results, with no specific current source-flagged threat, which the gate drops.

Generic risk-factor boilerplate naming climate change, adverse weather and natural disasters as possible impacts; it states no driver state, change, surprise, guidance or action, so the gate drops it.

Boilerplate risk-factor incorporation statement asserting no material change to previously disclosed risk factors; it names no driver state, change, surprise, guidance or action, so the gate yields no DriverUpdate.

Generic risk-factor boilerplate from the forward-looking-statements list: it names weather and climate change as things that could affect results, with no stated state, change, size, direction, guidance or action for this company or period, so it is a bare risk mention and yields no fact.

Generic risk-factor boilerplate: the sentence lists hazard types and says such issues 'have occurred and may occur within our system from time to time', with no specific, current, source-flagged incident, no value, and no state, change, guidance or action, so the gate yields no DriverUpdate.

Generic forward-looking risk-factor boilerplate listing food safety and food-borne illness risks: no stated state, change, surprise, guidance or action about a driver, and no specific current source-flagged adverse threat, so the gate drops it.
Generic ordinary-course litigation boilerplate: no specific proceeding, amount, stage, or change is stated, so it is a bare topic mention and the gate yields no DriverUpdate.
Pure cross-reference boilerplate pointing to risk factors in other filings; it states no driver state, change, surprise, guidance or action, so the gate yields no DriverUpdate.

Generic forward-looking cautionary bullet about the possibility of not realizing anticipated Space NK acquisition benefits: it states no current, source-flagged specific adverse threat and no actual state, change, guide, or completed action, so the gate drops it as risk boilerplate.

The $24.6 million is a NET roll-up spanning four independent causes (impairment of assets and lease termination expenses, FRC acquisition-related items, gift card breakage, and gift card inventory adjustments); one name may carry only one cause, the quote quantifies no individual component, and the measured quantity is therefore an accounting aggregate rather than a single driver, so the value cannot be lawfully assigned and the item is parked rather than guessed.

This is a generic forward-looking risk-factor listing inside the Safe Harbor statement naming weather and natural disasters as things that may affect results; it states no current condition, level, change, or event, so it is exactly the boilerplate the gate drops.

Generic forward-looking risk-factor boilerplate: it lists macroeconomic conditions, inflation, interest rates and cost pressures as things that could affect future results, with no stated state, direction, size, action or outlook for any driver, so the gate drops it as a bare topic mention.

Standard 10-Q risk-factor incorporation statement asserting no material change from the prior Form 10-K; it names no driver state, change, surprise, guidance or action, so it is generic boilerplate and yields no fact.

Bare topic mention inside the forward-looking-statements risk list: weather is named as a generic uncertainty with no stated state, change, size, direction, period or action, which the gate drops as risk boilerplate.
Generic forward-looking-statement risk boilerplate about unspecified risks and uncertainties; it names no driver state, change, surprise, guidance or action, so the gate drops it.
Standard forward-looking-statement safe-harbour and generic risk language; it names no driver, no state, no change, no guidance value and no action, so the gate drops it as boilerplate.

A real-sounding below-expectations claim that cannot be lawfully resolved: it names no company metric value or period-bearing home fact, and 'expectations ... from an industry perspective' is neither analyst consensus nor the company's own prior guide, so no surprise baseline can be stated without guessing.

Ungrounded expectation comparison: 'in line with expectations and guidance' names no identifiable metric, value, period or home fact in this quote, so no surprise fact can be grounded and no home sibling exists.
Generic forward-looking-statement boilerplate pointing readers to Form 10-K/10-Q risk factors; it states no driver state, change, surprise, guidance or action, so the gate drops it.

Generic forward-looking-statement and risk-factor boilerplate: it names no driver state, change, surprise, guidance or action, only that unnamed factors could make results differ, so the gate drops it.
Generic forward-looking safe-harbor boilerplate: it names no driver, no state, change, outlook, expectation comparison or discrete action, so the gate drops it as generic risk language.
Standard forward-looking-statements disclaimer: it states no driver level, change, outlook, expectation comparison or discrete action, so the gate yields no fact.

Ungrounded expectation claim: 'beat and raised' and 'exceeded on all metrics' name no identifiable metric, value, expectation operand or period, so no surprise can be grounded to a home sibling and no lawful fact exists.
Generic forward-looking-statements disclaimer boilerplate; it states no driver state, change, surprise, guidance or action and is dropped by the gate.
Call-logistics announcement of the next earnings release date and conference call; it says nothing about any driver's state, change, surprise, guidance, or action, so the gate yields no DriverUpdate.

group_collapses.reason: The single sentence states two different readings of different kinds — a dollar sales level above $11 billion and a percentage share of sales just under 60% — with different units and different drivers, so they are distinct facts that happen to share one locator.

The shared sentence states two alternative pricing options at the Company's election — a base-rate margin of 0.5% to 1.0% and a Term SOFR margin of 1.5% to 2.0% — which are different reference rates with different stated ranges, so they are distinct drivers rather than one fact.

The single sentence states two separable things — the delivered comparable-sales value versus last year and that value's position against the company's own guidance range — and the expectation rule requires the actual to be written as a metric home plus a distinct surprise record.

One sentence carries two distinct facts on different lanes — a present measured share of combined sales (metric, ceiling at 3%) and a separate forward longer-term aspiration for that same share (guidance, numberless) — so they are not one underlying fact.

The one sentence attributes the same 10% divisional core operating profit growth separately to two different brands, so it states two distinct facts that differ only in their slice (Taco Bell division versus KFC division).
